decisions.decision: A Rogue can apply Sneak Attack damage to a successful attack when the target has failed to detect or anticipate the attack, or when the target has an explicitly established vulnerability that the Rogue can exploit with a precision strike. Detection uses the shared awareness and detection mechanics. Other qualifying vulnerabilities are established by specific conditions, actions, features, or successful techniques. Advantage does not independently establish Sneak Attack eligibility. Each attack is evaluated separately.
decisions.decisionBasis: Owner explicitly approved this wording, 2026-10-23. This conceptual rule authorizes neither a complete list of qualifying vulnerabilities nor a finished awareness/detection runtime.

decisions.decision: There is no Sneak Attack-specific distance cap; an otherwise valid ranged attack may qualify at normal allowed range, including sniper attacks. A Rogue can Sneak Attack with **any weapon they are proficient with**, whether or not it has the Finesse or Ranged property, if the attack succeeds and meets the independently established detection-or-vulnerability requirement. No extra Disadvantage or Sneak Attack dice penalty is imposed solely for choosing another weapon type. Weapon Mastery retains its usual effects; it neither replaces proficiency nor independently creates Sneak Attack eligibility. Ordinary attack restrictions and modifiers still apply; weapon proficiency must be acquired normally. Spell attacks, unarmed strikes and unusual non-weapon attack categories remain for general-system reconciliation.
decisions.decisionBasis: Owner approved the proficiency-only alternative on 2026-10-23, explicitly replacing the former proficiency-with-Disadvantage or Mastery bypass rule; review against Dorks & Dice simple-versus-advanced shared-combat principles.

decisions.decision: Defensive Roll is a Rogue special-ability choice at one of the historical choice levels 10/13/16/19. If an attack would reduce the Rogue to 0 HP, the Rogue may expend their Reaction and the feature's single use to attempt a Dexterity saving throw. On success they remain at 1 HP instead of dropping to 0 HP from that attack. The use returns on completing a Long Rest, not a calendar-day reset. Because Uncanny Dodge also normally spends the Reaction, neither can use the same Reaction on one triggering hit. The numerical save DC and special zero-HP interactions are NOT approved here: these must be supplied by the shared resolution system before the feature is executable.
decisions.decisionBasis: Owner approved the assistant's proposed one-per-Long-Rest Reaction-based 1-HP Defensive Roll emergency-survival design on 2026-10-23. The proposal explicitly left the exact Dexterity save DC and special restrictions pending.
